[page[title]]

Coordinate relationship, opportunity and delivery activity around a shared account and pipeline record.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Companies, leads, contacts, opportunities and relationship activity.
  • Email, mailbox records, materials, imports and handoff packs.
  • Process definitions and instances, plus hosted import and agent-workflow entry points.

Why the boundary matters

Commercial and delivery work stays connected to the relationship history, evidence and next action instead of being fragmented across personal inboxes and spreadsheets.

How it fits

CRM is a key adjacent domain with its own library, Web host, HostedServices host, unit tests and acceptance tests. It is not yet composed into cCoder.Core, but is expected to join that composition as its integration and package boundary matures. It currently consumes cCoder.AI through a local sibling project reference.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.ClientRelationshipManagement on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.ClientRelationshipManagement" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddCrmPlatform(/* connection and platform options */);
builder.Services.AddCrmEntityStacks();
app.StartCrmPlatform();

Configure and run it

Configure ConnectionStrings:CRM, ConnectionStrings:CRMAdmin, SSO and the decryption key. The repository supplies a standalone Web host and HostedServices entry point for imports and agent workflows.

Consume the capability

Use the CRM OData controllers for companies, leads, contacts, opportunities, emails, materials, imports, handoff packs and process state. Consume cCoder.AI through the application workflow layer so relationship evidence and human control surround model output.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.ClientRelationshipManagement.git
cd cCoder.ClientRelationshipManagement
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
